  title = {Python code is type-checked with mypy in its default mode},

  decision = {mypy, in its default mode plus \texttt{check\_\allowbreak{}untyped\_\allowbreak{}defs}, checks \texttt{recommenditos/\allowbreak{}} and \texttt{tools/\allowbreak{}} in a pre-commit hook and in the required \texttt{Lint \& format} job.
Untyped third-party packages are ignored module by module, \texttt{pandas-\allowbreak{}stubs} is not installed, and a finding is fixed in the code, not silenced.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item No type checker: ruff and the tests catch a lot, but annotations drift unnoticed and a forgotten \texttt{None} shows only in a test.
\item basedpyright: infers types from pandas' source and sees more there, but reported 193 errors, mostly pandas noise, and agents would scatter \texttt{ignore} comments.
\item ty: 19 diagnostics, but at version 0.0.89 its rules change between releases and CI would be unstable.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} 307 of 350 functions in the package and tools carry a return annotation that nothing checked.
mypy reports 19 findings in 9 files, none a real bug: each is a value the code does not show cannot be \texttt{None}, or a library type.
An explicit check or \texttt{assert} fixes each one.
It has a pydantic plugin for the M4 API.
It sees every DataFrame as \texttt{Any}, so column names and dtypes stay with \texttt{schema.\allowbreak{}py} and the tests.},
